Fortunately, we found a public beach access parking near Hyatt that was hidden from public view (you have to find it carefully on Google Maps). The hotels have occupied most of the beach front leaving very little space for the beach. However, the beach is maintained very well probably by the hotels.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Calm, great snorkeling, less people
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our Hotel was just steps away. Could always find a spot. If you walk down to middle you will see where all the snorkelers are and jump right in middle of it.  FYI, sand is thick and gets everywhere not powder like.  Just be prepared. Loved it. Can watch the whales all day long right from beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Average and Accessible Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was a good beach with convenient access to shopping and multiple hotels. The beach was not large yet not crowded. It is right next to black rock, which is a prime diving spot and from which you can see an interesting and brief sunset ceremony.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A must-visit relaxing place that deserves to be on your hectic itinerary
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a great place to relax, enjoy the beach, snorkel at your own pace and dive from a 25-foot rock.There is a hotel behind that has a bar, where you can get drinks.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just gorgeous!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The is a fabulous area of Maui!  The beaches are clean and quiet!  Very family friendly!  Tons of resorts line this beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Most perfect beach ever with great shopping really close by @ Whalers. Black Rock is such a beautiful spot & offers world class snorkeling. We saw sea turtles every day. Tons of tropical fish. The sand is so soft & white - it’s literally the picture beach! We loved having lunch @ the Hula Hut which is located right on the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Kaanapali!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach! It’s definitely a beach you should come and check out if you’re not staying at a resort on Kaanapali beach. I recommend staying at a resort on the beach because they all have beach access. The sand is great and it’s a clean beach. The water is crystal blue!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach for swimming, relaxing and eating!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you're looking for a private beach, this is not the place. This is tourist central BUT that being said, everything you need is here. Umbrellas, beach chairs, excursions, restaurants and shopping are all right here! the water is beautiful!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: First time
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not crowded, fantastic sunset views. Snorkelling was a lot of fun and even got to see a turtle up close!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excellent, quiet beach. Sunset it’s beautiful to look at, waters are calm and transparent. Definitely a beautiful beach to relax.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Snorkeling and jumping from Black rock is awesome!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spent several hours snorkeling and jumping from black rock.  Also, we saw several sea turtles- amazing!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My heaven
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We would walk along this beach in the morning and watch the waves come in and people watch. Very relaxing to me

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous but CROWDED!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: All the hotels are gathered hear, and all the people too.  It's like going on a Carnival Cruise.  I'd go to Kapalua instead.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: White sand in Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A wonderful place to stay... Just like the picture. We stayed at the Westin Timeshare Villas and it was like coming home to Hawaii. The views and rooms and amenities made staying in Ka'anapail just perfect.. You can walk on the beach forever.. Paradise in reality . Mahalo

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to stay... and Black Rock end of the beach is beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed at the Kaanapali Hotel Beach and loved our north end of the beach! The sand and the water in near Black Rock were great for hanging out and for swimming. And I enjoyed walking the trail from the north end down all the way to the public beaches past the Hyatt everyday! Lot's of people... but if you like people watching it is fun! And Whalers Village has a couple good eating spots (Can we say "Monkeypod"!!!) and shops.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Overrated
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Why is this such a highly rated beach? Maybe it was just the day we stopped in, but it was not great. We like to be able to at least swim, snorkel, or boogie board. We could do none of that here. The surf was too rough, and the beach itself is long but narrow. We quickly packed it up and found a better beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Family Beach Day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our family had a great day at Ka'anapali Beach. To our surprise, there was ample free public parking available when we arrived ~10am on our weekday visit, and plenty of space on the beach within 100 yards of the main park/restrooms. COVID-times surely contributing to the reduced traffic. Good snorkeling from shore in a number of spots. Good beach sand that was perfect for burying our 9-year-old daughter in up to her neck. A bit windy as to be expected...it's the beach! We enjoyed walking along the boardwalk/sidewalk and seeing all of the resorts. Plenty of resort restaurants to grab lunch at, from ultra-casual food trucks to high-end restaurants.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice, sandy beach conventent to resorts.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lots of room, some shady spots unter the trees.  No surf to speak of, pretty good snorkeling.  Drop off at shorebreak is steep, keep an eye on the kids.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had a full day on Maui before leaving for  the big island in the evening.   Our Uber driver said we should visit Kaanapali beach and dropped us off there for a few hours.    Great afternoon spot. Beautiful beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Can't park!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is beautiful,  clear, nice sand, and the beach walk that runs thru the area is awesome. Big problem is there is very little parking. All beaches are open to the public but the hotels own 99% of the parking lots. They tout public parking in a couple of places and once you get there, good luck. There might be a total of 10 spots and of course they're all taken.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach and a great place to snorkel. The water is so clear and beautiful. We loved this beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach in this area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best beach we found during our stay in Maui. Lots of sand, few rocks and clear water. Lots of beach to walk. Not a lot of people so wasn’t crowded. People were surfing, swimming and snorkeling. Wish we had had our snorkels with us during this trip! Facilities (just bathrooms) and place to wash off.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: 1 of the best Beaches in the World
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful, peaceful beach. You can roam the beach without a lot of people. Current is a little rough, you just have to be careful of tides. Scenery is to die for!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hard To Beat This Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is one of Maui’s best. It’s approximately a mile long and borders numerous luxury resorts and condos. The extreme north end has famous Black Rock, which is known for cliff diving, great snorkeling and the island’s first mega resort, The Sheraton. The beach is widest in this area and gets much smaller on the south end. The best part may be the paved walkway that runs between the beach and the resorts.  This walk offers beautiful views, entry points to the beach and numerous restaurants and retail shops. There are also several rental kiosks where visitors can obtain snorkeling gear, beach chairs, umbrellas and surf boards. Restrooms are plentiful as are entryways to public parking for those not renting rooms at one of the resorts. Get here early if planning to rent beach or ocean related equipment. Expect to pay high prices for anything available to purchase or rent.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Researched ocean quality at Kaanapali
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The County of Maui is facing a fine by the EPA for their discharged wastewater containing sewer. This is concentrated at theKaanapali  Kahekeli Beach Park  and drifts North. If you are immune compromised or concerned, then Google for updates. Such a beautiful beach,  just use the beach section South of Kahekeli.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Drove out here during our stay in Maui.  We were in Wailea-Kihei area.  Took about 30-40 minutes.  The drive was gorgeous!  Be sure to stop at the scenic lookout spots to capture great photos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Walkway on the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We parked at Whalers Village ramp and walked the beach walkway for awhile. There is a lot to see. Hotels, restaurants, beach. Lots of activity. I recommend a visit. Parking is free for 3 hours if you get your parking voucher validated with a purchase. We made our purchase at ABC store. Be sure to see the whale bones in Whalers Village.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a gem - beautiful beach, grounds and outstanding friendly staff.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ka’anapli Beach Hotel (KBH) is a wonderful place to stay and experience Maui and the Hawaiian culture. We have stayed here 3 times - our honeymoon and two anniversary celebrations- and we hope to stay here many more times. The staff is very friendly and kind.  Many employees that we visited with have been with the hotel for 20 to 30+ years. The hotel treats both employees and guests very well. The hotel grounds are beautiful and the atmosphere is very relaxed.  Every employee we encountered was extremely nice.  The hotel has a department dedicated to providing free Hawaiian culture classes to hotel guests.  We stayed in the newly renovated Papakū wing in an oceanfront room.  The views were fantastic - like something out of a story book.  Sunsets were stunning, rainbows were frequent - all accompanied by the steady sound of the ocean just outside the door of our private lanai (balcony).  The room had simple clean lines, yet was very elegant, tastefully decorated and even included some crafts made by hotel employees.  If you are looking for a big name, opulent, gaudy hotel KBH isn’t for you.  But, if you are looking for gracious Hawaiian hospitality while you relax in beautiful surroundings then you will be very happy that you chose KBH.  KBH management and staff should be proud of the atmosphere that they have created and nourished.  I can’t think of a place I would rather be than KBH to relax and recharge.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was right outside our hotel, and it is gorgeous! Beautiful sunrises and sunsets!! The beach is also very clean, and it wasn't too busy while we were there for the week. Highly recommend!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It a Very Popular long skinny beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Its a great beach and offers very nice sunsets.  Just be aware it will be crowded.  Best to rent a beach cabana and camp out.  There are a ton of adventures you can sign up for and pay on the spot.  have fun  Aloha

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It is a great beach, just a lot smaller than we anticipated.  The water is beautiful and clear waiting for you to jump right in,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: I must be dreaming!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My favorite place is by the ocean, and I do believe Ka'anapali Beach has just become my all time FAVORITE place by the ocean - it's crystal clear blue/green waters with the mountains as the backdrop can NOT be beat!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach with something for everyone.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with something for everyone.  Great for surfing, walking, sailing, and cliff jumping.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful and gorgeous with lots of activities to enjoy for the whole family.  Lots of room to enjoy the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach on Maui despite local richey rich jerks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the beach to go to for your first trip to maui - good snorkeling, swimming, and sunbathing.  Lots of restaurants and bars and a great boardwalk.  We stayed at the maui kai which has no beach but is very close.  Our only issue was a local - probably a richy rich busy body that was on the beach serving as his own private beach patrol - yelling at people and accosting them for drinking beer, smoking, or not having dogs on a leash.  I am surprised this guy - dressed in black shorts and a black long sleeve shirt didnt get punched out for being such an a-hole.  Regardless of mr. local a-hole we had a great time and highly recommend

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is stunningly beautiful. It has fun waves, yet Black Rock stays pristine for snorkeling. We saw huge schools of fish and two green sea turtles. We love to arrive early (8 a.m.) to get a free parking spot in the small lot. If we arrive later in the day we park at Whalers Village and buy some macadamia chocolates or cold drinks from ABC store to validate our parking (only $15 for validation). When swimming in the evening, live music often floats down from the restaurants which makes for a magical atmosphere.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach for swimming, you can walk a long way on the beach. Not too crowded, hard to find any shade though. Snorkeling was great near Black Rock, saw a few turtles. Gets deep fairly quickly in spots.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Rich, Blue Waters of Ka'anapali
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a lovely beach. The water is very clean and clear, the West Maui setting is lovely, and it is long enough that you can find your spot and not feel crowded by others. You don't need to be a hotel guest to enjoy it; I wasn't. While the public parking lot is not huge, I found a space on the two occasions I tried. The beach is a fine, powdery white sand, but there are small rocks in the shallow surf, as well. Last time I was here, I spied 5 turtles in the water and one of them swam right into me. By all means, go.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Soft Golden sands, beautiful clear blue water , lined by palm trees 🌴. We really enjoyed this beach 🏝.The type of beach where your kids could play sand castle 🏰 & frisbee , swim 🏊🏼‍♀️ 🏊‍♂️, hang out all day. Bring your own beach chairs & umbrella.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: beautiful view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: the beach has a amazing view, the water changes colors and is very impressive, best part of my  the worst trip

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was a beautiful white sand beach.  The waves were big enough for kids to paddle out and boogie board, but too big for snorkeling from where we were at in front of the shops.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful blue waters, big waves.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Parked for free behind the Westin. Wind was strong and so were the waves. Super clear water and gorgeous white sand. Beautiful beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clear Blue Water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was a little hesitant to go there because I know it is a crowded and popular beach but I am so glad we went. We went around 11 and were able to find a parking spot in the Whaler's Parking garage. Beach was beautiful and clean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: near drowing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have been scubadiving/ diving /night diving/ for 30+ years.   ALMOST DROWNED-at Black Rocks.    We entered the water by the Sheraton Hotel.  Swam against the current going out- unfortunately we rounded the corner of the rocks- that was a big mistake. We swam for about 30 min.- decided to turn around- just starting to get to far. The current had changed- we were swimming again against the current.My mask started fogging- mistakely took it off temporarily to de-fog it .  gulped in some water...     was about 50 yards from the turning point back in- but couldnt get around- and couldnt see anyone to yell to.    fortunately , there was an outrigger  I yelled to - and they came to pick me up.   but not before i had the thought " I'm not gonna make it".  i had hyperventilated, i could no longer float- because of that, and i had tired out my arms and legs,   I REALLY thought i was done!!!  NO MATTER how comfortable you are in the water ( I am ), I was not prepared for the sudden wind change, the ferocious current, and relentless waves.      THANKYOU TOthe outrigger that saved my life -   my kids would have NEVER believed that i would drown.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is beautiful and serene. It extends for miles and is a very peaceful setting with a lot of marine life and views of different islands.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Miles of beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach walk along North and South Kaanapali Beach is beautiful.  If you are a runner, get up early and have it to yourself.  We walked in the morning and at night.  Every inch of this beach has a beautiful view and depending on where you stop you will find different beach ... sometimes rocky and full of coral ... other times, sandy and calm.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent beach for families with kids
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excellent beach for families with kids- parked at Whalers and validated at ABC- waves were perfect for boogie boarding.  Rentals on the beach and pricery. Nice rinse off area..

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice sand beaches. Next to all Kaanapali resorts.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Talk about convenience! If you're staying at any of the Kaanapali resorts, the beach couldn't be closer. The beach is clean. Waves are close to shore and provide lots of excitement. The grandkids wanted to go everyday. (Note: the grandkids said the pool was too boring.)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach Area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Maui in June 2021.  We booked a condo on the resort stretch of Kaanapali beach.  We highly recommend this area for families and those who are interested in a resort-style vacation (we are an active family and hiked quite a bit over on the Northern side so that was about an hour's drive away). The beach here is great for sunning, swimming, surfing, SUP - it is large and sandy as opposed to some beach area where there are rocks.  If you want to snorkel, you are within walking distance of a great area to snorkel and see turtles as well (May's Beach which is about a 16 minute walk from Whaler's Village), there are many amenities in Kaanapali  (spa services, sailing, parasailing, surf lessons, SUP, etc.).  There is a long and lovely paved beach walk as well that connects the resorts and condos to Whaler's Village, an outdoor mall with restaurants, ice cream, and shopping. If you like to be more "on your own" and don't care for the "resort feel" you may want to consider Paia or other areas on the North side. We really loved it over there as well - and it has a different feel to it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is beautiful. The ocean was much stronger than expected, the undertow was very strong. Be aware with children and older folks. The sunsets are breathtaking!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Calm waters and beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a lovely, long beach with no rocks.  It is a long beach with little waves, so terrific for children.  sand was soft through the toes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Do at least once
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a beautiful beach but crowded and usually with rough sea conditions. There are so many other beaches with less people and nicer conditions. Ka'anapali Beach is the place to see and be seen. For the past few years, there has been beach deterioration from swells. These swells have affected the entire West and Northwest beaches unless the beach is in a cove or bay. Good to go to and experience at least once.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Try going in the morning!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was hard to relax at this beach. Waves wore us all out as they constantly rammed us back into the beach shore! Probably related to us going in the afternoon and high winds the whole week in Maui. We later figured out that Maui wind (and subsequently waves) pick up jn the afternoon, so I would try going here in the morning. Go to The Snorkel Store website and sign up for daily snorkel/swim reports so you will know conditions before you go!Beach wise Kaanapali is really beautiful. We didn't get to go down to Black Rock to see if the water was any calmer. This beach connects to Whalers Village with easy parking there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ka'anapali Beach as beautiful as ever !  This was our 3rd trip there and it didnt disappoint.  Maui and its beaches are amazing !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Love Ka'anapali Beach, what an amazing beach, highly recommend... Rented chairs, umbrella.  Had several great days just relaxing on the beach enjoying the gorgeous views.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Continuously Well-Rated Beach Lives Up to Hype
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were blessed with a week long stay on the Kaanapali Beach at the Westin May 23-29, 2021. The beach was everything we could have hoped for and more. Clean, great sand, gentle waves but with enough places to still enjoy them either body surfing or watching others on boards, crystal clear waters, and plenty of space to walk up and down the beach enjoying the views of Lanai and Molokai. Hotels are doing a good job of limiting chairs and umbrellas currently, so this kept space open and enjoyable, but the place is definitely getting more busy :). Sunsets were gorgeous over the water and the islands, and morning sunrise walks were pure bliss.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Watch out for the rocks. Beautiful place to go play in the waves! The beach is really long with plenty of places to put your stuff.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice and clean beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach! Clean and not too crowded! It was better than I thought it would be! Exceeded our expectations and would recommend!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We spent quite a bit of time on this beach, largely due to our hotel's location here.  It was our favorite beach.  The sand and water were wonderful.  Great snorkeling a Black Rock at the end of the beach.  Gentle enough surf for kids but enough to play.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Okay, semi-artificial paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is very developed, with lots of resort hotels covering its scope.  Which means lots of manmade features and lots of people.  I personally found that it detracted from some of its natural beauty, which is indeed excellent ... think swarms of sea turtles swimming close to the sandy shore .

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Soft Sand and Great Views!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sand at this beach is silky soft and a beautiful yellow. To get to the beach you have to park in the commercial parking garage and then lug your stuff through the mall which wasn’t ideal but once you’re there it’s well worth it! If you spend more than $10 at one of the shops they’ll validate your parking. Otherwise you can spend up to $40 on parking if you’re there all day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach was clean & had a friendly atmosphere. We walked the beach & noticed certain vibes each part gave. There were calmer areas & there were busier/louder areas. Would definitely consider visiting again!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved this perfect view and great Sunset! You don’t need to pay for this beach and the beautiful beach views are priceless!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach; Minimal Surf
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This review is for Ka’anapali beach south of Black Rock. We enjoy parking at Whalers Village and setting up right in front of that area. Decent amount of sand from the ocean and close access to restrooms. Great people watching. If you are looking for fewer people and more scenic views, head toward South Maui.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Yes it’s a lot like every other great beach but
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s got everything- clear beautiful water, soft white sand (I wondered if it’s brought in bc the rest of the Maui beaches I’ve been too don’t have sand like this) and some nice shops and expensive restaurants just a stroll away.  And foot showers and restrooms.   I prefer some other beaches for a better Maui experience but this one is just so easy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach but bring Water Shoes
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was great but you need to pick your spots as it sits right on coral for most of it.  The walkway is very busy and everyone at the hotels/vacation rentals crowds around the pools and walkways so beach/sand is pretty empty.  I recommend camping out in front of the Westin as it was the widest part of beach with least amount of coral/rocks and still had decent waves.  Beware of the many catamarans that beach dock just past the Westin as they are constantly picking up and dropping off tour passengers and it can be a big unsettling while snorkeling.  I recommend walking down to the black rocks in front of the Sheraton as that is where the best snorkeling is or if you are up for it go to the other side of the Black Rocks for some great snorkel.  I thought all the food restaurants at Whaler's Mall were marginal.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Our favorite beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great for snorkeling and pretty quiet, less crowded. We always see a ton of fish and have swam with the turtles a few times

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Definitely worth a dip in the sea here in paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Saw a sea turtle within 5 minutes of entering the water! The water and wake was a little rough but for a strong swimmer on that somewhat windy day getting out to the coral reef made all the difference. Really clear water. Beautiful blue skies. Can't think of a better way to spend a morning than whiling away with the sea life in the beautiful, not too cold, waters off of Kaanapali beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect place to snorkel
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fun beach to snorkel at, people watch, jump off black rock. Watch out fir the waves that come in high in the afternoon.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the World's Best Beaches.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: There its a reason why Ka'anapali Beach was once the "playground" for Hawai'i's royalty and Ali'i. This area of Maui is stunningly beautiful, and is rich in the history and heritage of Hawai'i. The beaches are great! Wide open and safe. The resorts are also first-rate. Ka'anapali offers something for nearly everyone, but beach lovers will truly love this area. Swimming, snorkeling and cliff diving are top attractions at Ka'anapali Beach. However, at least on my visits over the last 30 years, there is not much in the way of surfing here. Surfers are better off traveling further up the westside of Maui (Kapalua, for example) for waves. Granted that Ka'anapali Beach can get crowded from time to time, but that shouldn't set you back too much. Just plan your visit carefully, and try to avoid "prime time." There are plenty of places to dine, shop and drink in the Ka'anapali Beach area. Although some of these places are on the expensive side, don't worry about it. Its only a 10-15 drive down to Lahaina town. In sum, there is really no downsides to Ka'anapali Beach or the local resorts. If you are planning to visit Maui, this is a wonderful area in which to base your vacation out of. Aloha & have fun in the "place of kings and queens!"

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Famous but over rated beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pretty beach, but it’s crowded and touristy. If you’re looking for snorkeling, skip this stop. Poor visibility and the crowds seem to scare off fish. We collected a bunch of trash out of the water.  Hotels have only super expensive food.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not enough people wearing masks, but nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Crowded over spring break and not everyone is wearing a mask on the boardwalk, with no enforcement. But a good beach with lots to do. I wouldn’t be surprised if there is an outbreak soon.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Kaanapali
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Day of relaxing , enjoying watching whales, lunch at hula grill. Current can be strong, no lifeguards,

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Stayed on the north side of Blackrock at the Westin and the snorkeling was best here.  Sometimes tricky to dodge the coral getting in and out but scout the sand entries before going.  Coral is sloooowly coming back so make sure to use "reef safe" sunscreen while you visit any of the Hawaiian islands.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turtles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s the busiest beach we visited but for the snorkels in our group it was the best.  They snorkeled around black rock and down the way they had the best visibility and they saw several turtles and a baby shark as well.  We even saw a turtles swimming along with the kids right at the beach.  After swimming and snorkeling we headed into the Sheraton Resort right there for drinks and lunch by their pool, we were welcomed in no problem you didn’t have to be a guest of the hotel to enjoy the bar.  FYI they also validate your parking which is quite expensive.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous beaches for miles. The boardwalk is great. Lots of great restaurants and shops along the way.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice but crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach. There were a lot of people not wearing masks even while walking along the sidewalk/boardwalk. If you're looking for a quiet beach, this one is not for you. We also experienced HUGE waves here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Right out of the Hotel
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the better beaches on Maui. Views of whales, great for people watching too. Got a bit windy later in the day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent snorkeling spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful underwater scenery right offshore. Calm waters off of Airport beach and the Westin Kaanapali resorts.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love this Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I love this beach because its wide, has soft golden sand, calm turquoise  waters and a magnificent view of Lanai and Molokai.  A great, easy beach to get to.  Bring your beach chair, a good book, and give yourself that treasured break you deserve!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful popular beach for everyone
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The central part of this beach has the widest beach area. Whales are common sights. Black Rock is great for snorkeling and listening to whale songs.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love Ka’anapali Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ka’anapali Beach is our favorite place to stay on Maui, numerous resorts, hotels, and condos; fabulous beach, excellent snorkel location (Black Rock), plenty of very good restaurants, and fairly central to most everything. Overall, don’t think you can do better.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: sweet beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lots of kids & families, yet enough room that you aren't on top of each other.  When we were there (Feb. 2021) we saw whales breaching in the distance.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great long sandy beach. Not sure why it's the best beach in Maui cause it not . But it is nice. There is limited parking by some hotel

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach but be prepared to pay for a beach umbrella if you can't be in the sun for hours. Very few shady  spots are all taken early in the morning.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Kaanapali Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We love this beach.  It’s never too crowded and we often walk down to Black Rock and jump off the rocks.   We even worked out on the grass in front of the ocean a few mornings.  There’s a nice boardwalk that stretches for miles.  The water feels very refreshing.  Highly recommend.  Steve Concialdi

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kaanapoli Beach is  beautiful.  It is gorgeous sand, not rocky at all.  It is safe for kids.  It is good for beginner surfers and boogie boarders!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand and Snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Long beach with plenty of sand and room for social distancing.  The reef is just off shore with plenty of fish during snorkeling.  Visited several times and found space in the free parking lot right on the beach near the Westin every time.  Showers and bathrooms right on the beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Little crowded but good beach scuba spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I took  my granddaughter here for Discover Scuba and we loved it (first time I dove from a beach - coral was ok but not as good as deeper dives from a boat)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but a little crowded for our taste
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My family (wife and two girls ages 5 & 7) visited this beach while we vacationed in Lahaina  for the holidays.  It's a very long beach where there are a lot of resort properties (Westin. Marriott, Ritz, Hyatt).  If you are staying at one of these properties you have direct and easy access.  We were not and we drove there.  We parked by the beach access point near the Hyatt and parking is very limited. This was during covid times so limited parking was not an issue though I would expect that during normal times it would be.  Due to the breach erosion We had to walk a few hundred feet to get to a point where there was significant beach area we could set up our chairs.  But that area was close to a group of resorts and there were lots of people there.  Note that this would not be an issue during normal times but we were trying to maintain social distance.  The beach was amazing and the view was spectacular.  When we took a break from the water we walked down the beachwalk to Whalers Village which is an outdoor mall with high end shops and restaurants.  We got the girls a treat from a gelato shop and returned for more fun in the water. We stayed until the evening and watched the most amazing sunset.   Though we did enjoy ourselves we preferred Kahekili Beach Park because it was much less crowded and did not have the erosion issue.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We chose this beach each day we were on Maui and wanted a beach experience. Pretty mellow and it has fun reefs to snorkel around. We had a great time just hanging out as a family. limited parking is the only drawback to going to this beach site.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Casual beech setting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My family and I enjoyed an afternoon on the sandy beaches of Ka’anapali. Aside from sandy beaches and a friendly snorkeling environment, Ka’anapali beach also offers some outstanding views of the sunset. Friendly turtles are within snorkeling range and offer a wonderful snorkeling experience. Will visit again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fabulous beach with turtles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was clean and easy to walk on. Turtles swam by often. We watched the sunset every evening from our resort Marriott vacation club. We would also see whales in the distance.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Good place to snorkel, waves were fairly small and the current was enough to move you around with little effort.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beach for everyone!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is so gorgeous and accessible to everyone.  There’s easy parking.  A wonderful path to walk on along the beach.  Showers to clean off.  You can hang out on the soft sand, go for a walk, snorkel, swim or paddle board in the clear, calm waters.  It’s truly paradise!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best Beach on the island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Love this beach! Our fav on the island and best and safest boogie boarding spot we’ve found. It is clean and swimmable too. There is also great snorkeling by Black Rock as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous beaches! Great snorkeling here as well. Perfect for swimming, lounging, or walking the coast or beachwalk

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the top Beaches on our Planet, Don't miss a visit if you are on Maui!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with nice waves. If the surf is BIG please be careful as the waves come down hard.  A long walk is always fun on this Beach, lots of Resorts along the way. Be sure to bring along your sun screen and a beach chair.  Aloha

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great swimming beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach for swimming. Not much for snorkeling unless you go to the far north end at Black Rock 🪨. Parking was easy because there were so few people because of COVID.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Chill
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Mild waters with scattered baby waves with one surf spot (at least). Packed by hotels. Lovely esp sunsets.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing Place to Spend the Day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We spent a couple of days sitting on the beach and doing some leisurely snorkeling.  Parking is convenient.  Not too busy but this visit was during the pandemic so under other circumstances, expect a crowd.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Just beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful white sand beach with amazing views of Molokai and Lanai. Less crowded past black rock.  Stay at the Royal Lahaina resort.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A Must see beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice beach! Definitely a place to check out during your Maui stay.  It might get tricky for small children if the waves are bigger ... parents be careful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Absolutely gorgeous. I could look at the water forever and swim in it forever. So warm and beautiful

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turtle city!!!  Everywhere!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Epic snorkeling like I've never seen before, and I've snorkeled a LOT of places!  Start at the Sheraton, look by the rocks just off the beach, and enjoy watching a bunch of sea turtles pick at the grass on the rocks. You can even stand here it's so shallow.  Then head out along the reef, around Black Rock, and find beautiful caves, black tipped reef sharks , more turtles , unicornfish, needlefish, etc etc etc.  Absolutely gorgeous!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach for swimming and snorkeling.  I have come back several times. I particularly enjoy eating and drinking at the restaurants along the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun snorkeling and lovely view
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had a great time snorkeling and playing in the sun. I highly recommend  this place. Great location.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sad
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Hardley any beach the hotels are stuff in too close to the water.No room for families and not clean

reviewsWithKeywords.title: These western Maui beaches really are paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We experienced this beach when we visited Whaler's Village.  Like the beaches a little north with Moloka‘i in the background this one has views of Lanai off in the distance.  Of course the sand is wonderful and the sound of the surf with just the right amount of wind makes these western Maui beaches everything that you hear about them.  Just beautiful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Our finest outdoor library
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This normally packed beach was completely empty at noon. The hotels lining it are closed, due to Covid, but the water’s still clear and inviting, and the soft sand beckons a long stroll to Black Rock. I don’t imagine this beach is ever unsatisfying, but empty, it helps you imagine a more pristine time. No waves to speak of, while I was there, but a great place to read.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice view of whales
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach, ample parking, facilitiesGreat place to watch the whales during the winter months and plenty of over priced shops nearby

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best beaches in the world with breathtaking views!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I did a review back in March.  I just wanted to upload some pictures of the Ocean View Suite that I stayed in.  I loved the room and really enjoyed my stay.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Solid beach but in a crowded area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is great if you're staying in one of the many nearby hotels, but don't fret if you miss it because there are certainly many more beaches throughout Maui that are more appealing in my opinion. The sand is super soft, the view is fantastic, and the water has the perfect temperament here. With all that said, it still doesn't crack my top 10 in Maui if you're willing to explore.  If you do visit, be sure to see Whaler's Village and walk the trail along the fronts of all the hotels.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good walking beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful long beach great for walking. We did venture in for a swim however there are lots of hidden rocks And coral that we didn’t see from the shore. It made it a little tricky for getting out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Our favorite beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Warm water, clean sand. This beach is perfect for a day of fun. We spent 10 days sitting under our umbrella, relaxing, and playing in the gentle waves.  Get ready Maui, we are coming back in October!!! 🌺🏖🐬

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Kaanapali Beach June 25 3:30 pm
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of Maui’s most beautiful beaches, even more beautiful without the crowds. Right now there is plenty of free parking!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Sand and Water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our resort was located right on Ka’anapali Beach. We watched the humpbacks and dolphins swimming almost every day. The beach is a great location to relax and enjoy the Maui sunshine! The beach and surrounding area were very clean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Kaanapali beach: best place to people watch
reviewsWithKeywords.text: In the heart of all the Kaanapali action. A number of great restaurants and Whalers Village mall right next door. A beautiful family friendly beach. Good snorkling to the north by black rock. Super golden soft sand and lots of room to spread out. Nothing like a mai tai at Leilanis or the Hula Grill to help you relax. Heavenly!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ka'anapali is an absolutely beautiful beach.  We never went into the water here since our resort had a nice pool but we did see plenty of people hanging out on the beach and/or playing in the water.  At one point, we did go down to the water and take pictures.  It never seemed that busy, probably because of how large it is and that it's flanked by resorts with pools.Granted, it's not the beach specifically but we saw whales daily while walking on the beach (or the boardwalk).  We didn't see any whales while at Wailea so this area is pretty special to see them (during the right time of the year). Further North on the beach, we saw places you could rent snorkel gear, chairs, etc.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Without The Crowds!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Due to the Covid-19 Pandemic and the associated a Hawai’i restrictions on travel and stay-at-home requirements - except essential tasks, including exercise - Kaanapali Beach, Whaler’s Village and all the hotels that line the shore is a virtual ghost town.It’s an amazing experience to walk the beach path and swim in the ocean as the only people on the beach for hundreds of yards, on a bright, sunny, Hawaiian afternoon on one of Maui’s most popular and crowded beaches and resorts!Photos are of the beach looking North, looking South, the KBH, and Whaler’s Village.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Soft sand, clear water and beautiful sunset
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best beach I’ve been to so far (and I live on an island). The sand is sparkly and soft, the water is crystal clear and has a perfect temperature.It’s a relatively long beach, so there’s enough room for everybody to relax in their own space.My husband and I were there last February and were delighted to see a few whales swimming there. (Of course not too close to where we were swimming, but close enough to be seen with the bare eyes.) The sun also sets beautifully at this beach.If you want to relax on soft sand, swim comfortably in clear water and enjoy a romantic sunset, this is the place to be.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach, warm water and great snorkelling, Beach was never crouded and could always find a great spot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This a beautiful stretch to beach above black rock and Kaanapali resort and hotel area. It has restrooms and showers and a wonderful boardwalk, just off the white sandy beach, that you can wander along for miles. Snorkeling is also good here and most of the time you will see scuba divers in the area too. Plenty of parking and just a great place soak up some sun and enjoy the day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Whale Soup in February!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We love Ka'anapali Beach and for the first time we were able to visit in February.  There is a walkway along the beach which seems to go on forever.  The sunsets are beautiful and in February we were able to see so many whales everywhere!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautful and Spacious
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed at the Westin and this beach is beautiful and big. You don't feel crowded at all. The water wasn't too bad for my 7 year old either. Not bad snorkeling either.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Breathtaking views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with a walkway that is approximately 5 miles long. Water is warm and good for snorkeling and scuba diving. And of course, people watching. Picnic tables and restrooms are available. Parking is limited so arrive early. There was a small craft fair on the grounds of one of the hotels just off the beach that was within walking distance.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ka'anapali Beach Grill
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were staying here and the restaurant was amazing. We ate there 9 or 10 times for breakfast, lunch, dinner and happy hour. the portions were large, the staff was supper friendly, and the food was amazing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach with good snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed nearby and enjoyed snorkeling this beach.  Parking was usually full by 9, so we walked over and spent the morning in the water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Entered the beach at Whaler's Village (stores and restaurants abound) . Actually saw a whale while wading at the shoreline. Lahaina has a good public transportation system (bus) which stops numerous places including Whaler's Village. All day pass for $4 can't be beat.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We love to snorkel and found things further north mostly too rough and murky so we tried this beach.  We saw many turtles and lots of fish.  The coral isn’t quite as healthy close in but gets better father out.  Around black rock there are tons of fish.  It was murky on the north side when we went so didn’t go all around.  One tip is to walk the beach first.  We thought we were fine to drift and come in anywhere and ended up coming in on rocks and getting scraped up.  So just be sure you know where you want to come back to shore.  Lots of sand, a lovely beachside boardwalk for much of the way.  Great shopping at Whaler’s village and parking (make sure you get validated).  The Westin has some great free beach parking.  Speaking of the Westin (I think there are 3) they do a great job in providing access for the public and take such good care of the boardwalk.  If I come back I would stay there just because they really try to keep things nice for all of the visitors, not just their guests.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Miles of great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great sand beach and not too crowded. We enjoyed many hours of swimming and tanning. good for families

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, good place to see sunsets. Nice walking path. Check out the torch lighting and diver off Black Rock every night a bit before sunset.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hearing and seeing the whales about 100 yards off the beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach wide and long.   Some snorkeling near black rock, out in the ocean side is a bit better.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is beautiful and a popular whale watching location. There are lots of swimmers in the water. I love the sidewalk that runs along the beach. Many restaurants and shops can be visited as well

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Ka anapali for my BD!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is so clean warm and inviting! a close walk from our hotel, water holds all the beauty we usually spend all day there, the sunsets are gorgeous

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful island views
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Rough waves and kids 10 and 13 weren’t keen on swimming or relaxing in the water but good for boogie boards. Great beach to walk. Soft sand. Beautiful views of the islands. Nice boardwalk along the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Whales, Cliff Divers, and beautiful scenery
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best places on Maui to go to the beach - we traveled all around the island and should have stayed at our own hotel beach.The best part was sunset tiki torch lighting at black rock, a glass of wine, and whales breaching right out from where we were.Surf conditions were rough and it was so windy we got sand blasted (winter in Maui) but loved it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the Best Beaches on the Island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach has it all - great sand, surf, and nearby snorkeling, great dining options nearby, and clear water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a great place to stay, play and snorkel at.  We stayed at the beach hotel, enjoyed the luau they have and also went snorkeling. It was all amazing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best beach in west Maui
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach goes on forever and ever. It is just a wonderful sandy beach with tons of room; it’s never crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kaanapali Beach is one of the most beautiful beaches on Maui.  A variety of activity options are available on this long and lovely beach.  In addition to the beach itself, the walking path paralleling the beach is also very enjoyable for leisurely walk or for exercise.  A not to be missed beach in Maui.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Long Beach 🏖
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach for walking or swimming. Neither undertow nor currents the day we were there. At north end of beach is Black Rock which is a great snorkeling spot! I know you’ll think I’m greatly exaggerating but we swam in a school of hundreds and hundreds of wrasses! Many eat in or take out restaurants at Whalers Village.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: 50th Anniversary
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is just perfect!  Beautiful sand, clean, lots of activities, such as surfing, kayaking, paddle boarding, and cafes.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best in Maui
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Exactly the beach you dream of when traveling to Maui.  Gorgeous sunsets and not too crowded. Lots of whale watching from the shoreline and nice walking path.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great location and beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great location and beach. Near enough to restaurants and things to do while being a great location to relax and enjoy the surf and sun. Have been here before adnbhioe to come back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Our favourite beach this side of the island.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with a GORGEOUS sunset! The ocean was a bit rough but not intimidating at all. There’s a lot nearby too. If you’re on this side of Maui I highly recommend taking some time to enjoy this beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Long stretch of beach!  Not a calm beach but very clean and nice!  Fun to walk the path along this beach, you can sit anywhere along the beach off the path!  Its connected to Whalers Village which is nice too, grab some treats do some shopping!  Lots of good restaurants along the beach too!  My suggestion go to those early less busy!!  Over all really like Kaanapali Beach!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Long stretch of sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This long stretch of sand runs for a couple miles along west Maui shores north of Lahaina. You can access the southern end of it at Kahekili Beach park which has decent snorkeling. There is also good snorkeling at Pu'u Keka'a (Black Rock) in front of the Sheraton on the beach and north of Whaler's Village. The beach extends even further to the north to Ka'anapali Point, where a reef in front of the Marriott offers some decent snorkeling as well. It is possible to park at hotel lots and pay the hotel for parking or park at Whaler's Village and stop by there to eat and shop at the end of your day. The businesses can validate your parking for up to 4 hours so you are responsible for the rest. Pay at the machines before you exit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Kaanapali No Ka Oi
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We love Kaanapali Beach, great views, walks, snorkeling and kayaking.  Not a great surf spot though.  In the winter can be windy, but you can see whales right from the beach! More family oriented than other parts of Maui and Lahaina is close!Best sunsets, IMHO, especially in the summer when it happens between Lanai and Molokai

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, clear water, soft sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of our favorite beaches!  First time to this beach. We have visited other Hawaiian beaches as well as some beaches in Caribbean.  This is tied as a favorite.  Here’s why: 1) the sand is soft on your feet, you don’t need water shoes to enjoy2) crystal blue water was clear as can be so you feel safe 3) family friendly beach, but not overcrowded4) in February we could sit beachside and watch the whales putting on a show easily - don’t even need to go on a cruise5) very clean6) gentle waves

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Clean but $$$
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is open but if you check into one of these hotels you'll be spending big bucks. Access to beaches is generally open but all the good spots are taken by the hotels.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Snorkeling Spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a treat if you are staying on Ka'anapali Beach.  You don't have to get in a vehicle to enjoy some of the best snorkeling with colorful fish and turtles.  Easy beach to enter the ocean with low waves.  Nice long beach for a stroll.  You can rent chairs and umbrellas if you wish or bring your own.  Plenty of spots for everyone.  With luck you'll also be able to watch whales near by.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Adventurebuddies42 goes to Ka’anapali beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Every time we go to Maui we either stay or definitely visit this beach. It has everything from a beautiful beach, many hotels, restaurants and activities. You can surf, go on catamarans, kayak, paddleboard... so many options. Even if you just want to sit on the beach and relax. Highly recommend!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous beach and the sunsets are beautiful and breathtaking! I will be back next year for sure to relax more as this year is done. February is the perfect time because of whale birthing and mating season you see the whales all day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect beach day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ka'anapali beach is perfect for relaxing in the sun with family and friends.  We were here in February during the whale season in which over ten thousand whales visit the bay between Maui and the neighboring two islands.  It was wonderful to drink the morning coffee while watching the whales in the distance.  It is highly recommended that you bring a binocular for a closer view.  The water is not as clear for snorkeling as some other beaches, but it is still possible to see a good variety of fish here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice day out
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kanapali beach is very pretty with big hotels. It is the older area with big hotels , we visited two of them 34 years ago, when there were only two. Now the Wailea area with the big new hotels is nicer than Kanapali Beach. Beach is great , white soft sand and public for everyone to use. You can eat at any of the hotels on Kanapali as they have nice terraces overlooking the beach. Fun day out there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A week with friends.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fantastic location for a relaxing and enjoyable holiday getaway with friends. Lots of restaurants and shops within walking distance and the beaches are fabulous. There is also a wonderful golf course right by the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: mesmerizing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: beautiful  sand beach that is so thick you can wade in it   easy entry to the sea without a lot of lava rock

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best whale watching from shore
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach to relax and enjoy. So fun to see whale activity from shore. Lots of breaches.  People stopping to watch.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Long stretch of beautiful beach; plenty of room so you're not on top of each other. Plenty of vendors if you want or need to rent any beach equipment. Snorkeling at Black Rock was so-so compared to other places.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach facing Lanai and Molikai.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great way to spend the day, sitting on Kaanapali Beach. Snorkeling is terrific. Turtles, eels, and lots of fish!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Afternoon Beach visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We come to this beach every year we stay on Maui.  It is very clean, has picnic tables and a area attached to the bathrooms that you can host a family function.  I would caution you to wear aqua socks if you're going in because there is coral outcroppings in the sand that will cut bare feet and give you a possible infection.  It is very pleasant and relaxing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My wife and I rode scooters out of Lahaina to Ka'anapali Beach. The scooter ride was fun...the beach break was awesome. Blue sky, warm temps, calm waters, soft sand. What more could a person ask for? Plus, there were crystal clear views of Lana'i and Moloka'i. Well worth a visit if you are on Maui.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beyond Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I stayed at the Hyatt Regency on Ka’anapali Beach. It’s simply breathtaking. The water is crystal clear, the sand is the softest I’ve ever felt, and the views of the nearby islands is just lovely.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice-looking Beach hard to swim
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were here in September and red flag warnings were out. The waves were pretty high and you had a hard time waiting out in the ocean. Went up to Black Rock to do some snorkeling but once again the waves would knock you over. I think if I was to go there again I would go to Honolua Bay instead.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not ALL of Ka’anapali Beach is great
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked the entirety of Kaanapali & Kahekili (North Kaanapali) Beaches, and swam and snorkeled in many spots. In my opinion, only the northern part of Kaanapali (Kaanapali Alii to Black Rock) and southern part of Kahekili (Black Rock to Maui Kaanapali Villas) are excellent, particularly if you prefer frolicking barefoot. In the other areas, rocks and coral present hazards. Guard against foot injuries by wearing water shoes. I saw a guy limping out of the water with a bloody foot near the Hyatt.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing views, but be safe in the water
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach with tremendous views in every direction.  The water depends on the season.  We have experienced some really rough surf in the winter months, which is to be expected.  That said, if it is too dangerous to swim or play in the water, all is not lost.  Maybe we have just been very fortunate, but it seems like a trend that when the water is rough, the view is not.  Witnessing the pure force of Mother Nature is more than enough, but we have noticed an added bonus that has been our experience at the very least; the beautiful humpbacks like to frolic and play in the rough water.  We seem to have more sightings when the weather isn’t perfect.  We love Ka’anapali.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach! Parking somewhat limited. Great view and walkway
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Really nice beach. Well maintained. Next to two other beaches. Need to get there early for best parking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Waves for days.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Best beach I have ever been to. We had a blast playing in the waves. My little guy played in the sand for 2 hours. Wife lost her sunglasses in ocean so she was not as enthusiastic as I was but I did warn her before she went in. You could hear the whales in the nearby waters of you put your head down to listen.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A perennialfavourite
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What is not to like about a broad white sand beach with gentle surf and coral close to shore! Ka’anapali Beach has it ALL! You can walk on a boardwalk, snorkel, build sandcastles and enjoy the beach park amenities (picnic, showers, change/toilet facilities, grassy area) of the Airport Beach Park (Kahekili Beach Park.) This is a favourite place for visitors and locals!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing & Snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Many days for the 10 we were in Maui were spent on this very relaxing beach! Relaxing and snorkeling, relaxing and snorkeling, relaxing ... You get the gist.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the best beaches in the world
reviewsWithKeywords.text: this is an excellent beach.  It is great for swimming, snorkeling and just watching the waves.  In winter you can also see whales breaching right from the beach.  Great sunsets.  A boardwalk that goes for miles and has many good restaurants.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A day at the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: What a lovely beach it is. It is pretty long which makes it a great place to go for a walk and half way through there is a great place to just off the lava rocks into the water. The surf on kaanapali can be a little strong in places so it is best to keep a close eye on younger kids.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach is beautiful and surprisingly clean. It's steep, and the wave action can be a little rough, so watch the kiddos if they're in the water. However, we saw turtles, humpback whales and lolos (little flying fish) just by sitting on the dry sand. The sunsets were incredible, night after night, with surprising colors.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Kaanapali Beach is incredible! From snorkeling at Black Rock (near Sheraton) to boogie board & SUP (Stand Up Paddle Board)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Awesome beach. Incredible views. Manageable waves and beautiful sand. Whales are bouncing around. Pretty awesome.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous great water and whales
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We love the beach the atmosphere the relaxation. Never disappointed and our go to beach for walking or ocean dipping.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty But Not Easy Swimming
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach with a fantastic view.  There is a path/ sidewalk stretching most of the beach. It’s fun to walk and look at all the hotel properties. The bad thing is there is very little beach, and it is quite slanted. This is not a great beach for swimming. Non the less, Kaanapali Beach is the place to be.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fine Clean Sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Peaceful in the early morning but many tourists enjoying the beach later.  Warm water but strong tide pull.  Went snorkeling near Black Rock and saw a variety of fish.  Easy to rent gear for 1-2 hours.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: We loved this side of Maui.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved this side of Maui. The beach was beautiful and we went snorkeling 5 times and loved the fish and the reef. The waves were calm enough for us to have our twin 7-year-olds out with us. Such a beautiful area!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Picnic tables, restrooms, changing facilities, palm trees, walkway, shaded parking, FREE. Easy access and very well kept up. Great people watching.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely place for lunch and a stroll.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great place to sit on the sand or stroll along the paved walkway in front of hotels....especially in the evening before sunset when the torches are lit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous beach and loved whalers village. Fantastic hotels to stay at at ka'napali and woukd definitely go back again.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: love this beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: passed a few days on these beaches.nice and clean with lots of room. they are never crowded. the water is beautiful and the sun is intense. can not go wrong !

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach in a great area!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved Kaanapai Beach! So much to see and do in the area. Loved walking along the beach and ain’t the boardwalk to whalers village to get a break from the sun when needed. The beach is beautiful and the water was no nice. Waves got crazy big while we were there too!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful walk on the boardwalk or the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I arrived into Lahaina on a very stormy day.  As such, our surfing lessons had been cancelled, so we decided to go to Kaanapali for a walk, and it did not dissapoint! First of all, Ka'anapali is only a five minute drive from Lahaina.  We parked in the public beach access point just before reaching Ka'anali, and walked the boardwalk from there.  This is a very well kept and clean walk with beautiful views of the ocean.  On the way back we decided to walk on the water.  The nice part about Ka'anapli Beach is it is a continuous stretch of sand (unlike Wailea) so you can walk the whole thing via the beach if you want.  There are also a number of stops you can make, like visiting the hotels, Ululani shaved ice, or Hula Grill.  An easy but beautiful walk that I highly recommend if weather is not allowing for ocean time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Plenty of room on this beach which goes on for miles. Easy access and plenty of parking if you are willing to look for it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Absolutely Beautiful.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Every beach we drove to see, we had a nice time but wanted to get back to "our" beach. Ka'anapali! The sand is soft, the ocean is kind, lots of room, great for snorkeling.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: One of the most beautiful beaches on the planet
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The views of Lana’i and Molokai, the gentle waves, the abundance of whales, surfers and boogie boarders, turtles feeding in the shallow surf and the miles of warm, soft sand make this one of our favorite beaches anywhere. This beach has something for everyone.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful; Best of Maui
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of our favorite beaches in the world. Walk for three miles on soft sand. Snorkel at Black Rock. Visit hotel pool bars. Rent gear. Boogie board when waves pick up. Spot whales during migration season (Dec - Mar) and listen for their song underwater.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lots of room to spread out. Waves are not too rough to swim in. If you get bored, you can go and shop in Whaler’s Village. Nice restaurants on the beach to eat at. Have the nachos at Leilani’s!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have visited a number of beaches around the world and this remains one of my favourites.Take the opportunity to explore this truly wonderful waterfront on one of the most beautiful Islands in the world.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, great views, we even saw whales in the water. The beach is clean and not too busy, great spot!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded beach with big waves and very strong undertow!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Grown adults were having difficulties at this beach getting into and out of the water when we were there in December/January.  Insanely big waves for a "relaxing beach".  The parking is almost impossible if you arrive after about 10AM.  Very busy beach ... the whale watches and tours take off right from this beach, so there is a constant flow of boats coming in and out and people walking through the beach to get to their excursions.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed at the Royal Lahaina Resort which is on this beach and it was amazing! Such a beautiful place. I definitely recommend going here :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice stretch of the beach, Easy access to restaurants and shops, busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed one of the resorts on the beach. It’s perfect location to walk, lots of beach sports to offer - it seems it’s good place for beginner surfers as waves are calmer than other locations in Maui. You can find plenty restaurants/shops to choose from at Whalers. I may not choose this to relax as there were so many people, but if you are looking for the location that is convenient to eat/clean up after swimming in the ocean, this is really nice place to go. We saw lots of youth jumping from Black Rock beach - it looked fun, but again it’s super crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach, complicated logistic
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I like this beach, tan sand, beautiful blue water. However it was a little crowded, there are a lot of resorts around and for us was very difficult to find a public parking lot -the one we found had around 20 spots. It doesn’t have public showers, restrooms or changing rooms, so if you are not staying in one of the resorts around will be difficult to hang out in here for the day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Snorkeling just off the beach was amazing with lots of colorful fish and sea turtles! Clean and not too crowed! No sand fleas...at least when we were there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach, with turtles!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Swam and snorkelled here. Safe and fun for swimming, and we also snorkelled, and saw loads of reef fish and several sea turtles.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Kaanapali Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is very beautiful and if you are lucky you get to see whales. Great for relaxing and enjoying the sun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Go NOW!!!!!!!!!!!!! This is a great area for you and the family. Strongly recommend the WESTIN North Ka'anapali villa as a respit for you and family too.Arch

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was our favorite beach near the Lahaina area! We went by the mall entrance, would highly recommend

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Airport Beach has great snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This Beach has great reefs, coral and lots of fish to see. Located near the Westin villas and Royal Lahaina Resort.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach for snorkeling and people watching. Greatestsunsets.  Near golf, tennis, shopping, spas and greatrestaurants.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Although very busy, this is a beautiful beach to visit and you can also walk along the beach boardwalk and visit many restaurants.  At the far right, they have a place for people to jump in off cliffs!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach for Snorkelling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Came here multiple times during our stay. Beaches aren’t too crowded. Large parking lot close to the beach with washrooms and change rooms on site. Sand is great and the tides aren’t too strong which made it great for swimming and snorkelling.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach with black rock
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is very beautiful and busy because of black rock which is used a lot for cliff jumping and snorkeling.Water has an under tow so be carefel. Lots of people in december/ january. Close to lots of shops and stores.Recommend it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but go early!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I are early risers so I feel that we get the best of Maui beach is before the crowds! This is a lovely stretch of beach and very easy for those less confident in the water as the entire Bay provides a Sandy entrance. Far over to the right is Black rock, some very basic snorkelling snorkelling. And when I say basic, I mean people who are snorkeling for the first time, have little to no snorkeling etiquette, and tend to flail around with their fans getting close to the one turtle they are attempting to chase. Hence, why we go early. If you do want to have a relaxing snorkel out around the point definitely try and get there between 830 and nine. By 10 AM the entire beach is full. The Sheraton on the far right does have public washrooms, and area to rinse off, and snorkel rentals if you don’t have  your own. They also have the beachfront overpriced cocktails that come in a small plastic glass for you to take back to your beach chair. I lovely beach but if you are like us and don’t want the crowds, go early!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach to spend the day. There are nice restaurants around in Whalers Village. Bit expensive but is decent. Sunset was nice. But note that the sunset will not be directly into the ocean eventhough it is west coast. There are mountains right around. Still it is beautiful to catch the glimpse of sunset sitting in the beach restaurants. Decent place to spend a day

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Manufactured Mother Nature with golf course
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Too many people with no aloha spirit. Other guests are in their own bubbles. Bad architecture and definitely geared to make money on everything. Food places pretty good! But amenities were disappointing and overbooked and underwhelming. What mother did was beautiful but faux waterfalls and tropical gardens not very tropical are not my scene especially crammed in between concrete to hide the concrete! Plus all the palm trees like it’s california on rodeo drive , it’s sad. And the need for grass on the beach is silly! But if boring hotel rooms with views and lack luster condos with plastic flowers is your idea of paradise-come on down...please don’t forget the HOA fees for that. I know low maintenance and modern like 1970’s please feel to come to bland suburbia in paradise just take a drive to Lahaina and see real paradise!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: great sand, great surf
reviewsWithKeywords.text: this is one of the nicest beaches on the island with great sand, waves and lots of amenites close by.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This review is for the Ka'anapali Beach Walk
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Ka'anapali Beach lies primarily between the Canoe Club (by the 1800's plantation workers' cemetery) to the large parking lot by the old Embassy Suites which is now a Diamond Timeshare property (look for the pink pyramid).  In between this walk along the beach is the Sheraton Black Rock.  Go through the hotel lobby to circumvent the rock; walk until you get to the beach end of the golf course and resume the walk.  This entire walk, start to finish, will be about 2 1/2 to 3 miles of a most delightful walk.The path will vary from flagstone, concrete, and wooden boards; it will wind its way along the beautiful coastline.  A large grassy public park lies close to the Diamond timeshare terminus with picnic tables, a restroom/shower, and grills.  There will probably be a craft fair set up somewhere along this stretch  The various hotels and resort cafes & shops (and also Whalers Village) provide for side trips along the route. More of the activity and rental kiosks lie on the stretch of beach walk between the Hyatt and the Westin hotel complexes.   Along our walk, we watched outrigger canoes ply the waves, catamarans go out on snorkel/whale watching excursions, and loads of beginner surfers and boogie board enthusiasts making their own memories.  Sometimes it becomes necessary to walk single-file in narrow parts of the path (which is likely to be the vast majority of the walk way).Always be on the lookout for the unexpected: beautiful birds, a little still life made from lost toys, an amazingly vibrant hued lizard, sea turtles (especially if the surf is calm) eating moss on the rocks, and sparkling sand welcoming the ocean's clear turquoise waters.  This is our favorite place on Maui (Ka'anapali Beach) and nearly everything we want can be found along this beach walk.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach, nice and peaceful. Clean, pretty sand. Some surfers when there are waves so they are fun to watch.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place but limited parking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is one of the best... shower located close to beach.  Snorkeling is decent.  Turtles usually around the south shore.  Fairly protected from waves and wind.  The beach sand is fantastic so great for kids.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing vacation!!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is amazing, has a lot to offer , no matter if you are with family or not can fit you!! , Furthermore the food is marvelous!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Few word of advice - save $$$
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A. Bring your Costco card wit you or get one specially for this trip, gasoline at the pump is $3.80 to over $4 VS Costco gas at $3.10 right there is $10-20 each time to fill up.B. Do you or the kids like Acai ? So a small size bowl on any of the islands is $9 to $11 or more - crazy ? Yes ! But it's only $4.99 at the Costco cafeteria

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Maui Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Calm water, sandy beach.  One of the top beaches on the island. Various access points and hotels are on this beach.
